questions.solution:
Let $A$ be the origin $B$ on $x -$axis, $C$ on $y -$axis,

So on plotting the diagram we get,

Now equation of circumcircle is given by

${\left(x - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Required equation of circle touches $AB$ and $AC$ and have radius $r$ so its equation is given by,

${\left(x - r\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - r\right)}^{2} = {r}^{2} ⋯ \left(2\right)$

Now given circle in equation $\left(2\right)$ touches circumcircle internally, so by property distance between the centre will be equal to modulus of difference of radii,

So, ${d}_{{c}_{1}{c}_{2}} = \left|{r}_{1} - {r}_{2}\right|$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{1}{2} - r\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - r\right)}^{2} = {\left(\left|\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} - r\right|\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4} + {r}^{2} - r + \dfrac{9}{4} + {r}^{2} - 3r = {\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}} - r\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{r}^{2} - 4r + \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} + {r}^{2} - \sqrt{10}r$

$⇒ r = 0$ or $r = 4 - \sqrt{10} = 0 . 837$

questions.q: Consider a triangle $PQR$ having sides of lengths $p, q$ and $r$ opposite to the angles $P, Q$ and $R$, respectively. Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE?
options: If $p < q$ and $p < r,$ then $cosQ > \dfrac{p}{r}$ and $cosR > \dfrac{p}{q}$
questions.solution:
(A) Applying cosine rule

$cosP = \dfrac{{q}^{2} + {r}^{2} - {p}^{2}}{2qr}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{q}{r} + \dfrac{r}{q}\right) - \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2qr}$

We know, using $A . M . \ge G . M .$

$\left(\dfrac{q}{r} + \dfrac{r}{q}\right) \ge 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{q}{r} + \dfrac{r}{q}\right) \ge 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{q}{r} + \dfrac{r}{q}\right)\dfrac{- {p}^{2}}{2qr} \ge 1 - \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2qr}$

$⇒ cosP \ge 1 - \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2qr}$

(B) $\left(p + q\right)cosR \ge \left(q - r\right)cosP + \left(p - r\right)cosQ$

$\left(pcosR + rcosP\right) + \left(qcosR + rcosQ\right) \ge \left(qcosP + pcosQ\right)$

using projection formula

$q + p \ge r$

Which is true as sum of two sides of triangles is greater than third side.

(C) $\dfrac{q + r}{p} < \dfrac{2\sqrt{sinQsinR}}{sinP}$

$\dfrac{q + r}{p} < 2\sqrt{\dfrac{sinQsinR}{\sin^{2}P}}$

Applying sine rule

$⇒ \dfrac{q + r}{p} < 2\sqrt{\dfrac{qr}{{p}^{2}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{q + r}{2p} < \sqrt{\dfrac{qr}{{p}^{2}}}$

Applying $A . M . \ge G . M .$

$\dfrac{\dfrac{q}{p} + \dfrac{r}{p}}{2} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{qr}{{p}^{2}}}$

So, (C) is not true

$⇒ \dfrac{q + r}{2p} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{qr}{{p}^{2}}}$

(D) $p < q$ & $p < r$

$⇒ p$ is smallest side

Let $cosQ > \dfrac{p}{r}$ and $cosR > \dfrac{p}{q}$ is true

$⇒ p < rcosQ$

$p < qcosR$

adding both inequalities

$⇒ 2p < rcosQ + qcosR$

using projection formula

$⇒ 2p < p$

$2 < 1$

Which is not correct.

questions.q: Let $x, y$ and $z$ be positive real numbers. Suppose $x, y$ and $z$ are the lengths of the sides of a triangle opposite to its angles $X, Y$ and $Z$ respectively. If $tan\dfrac{X}{2} + tan\dfrac{Z}{2} = \dfrac{2y}{x + y + z}$, then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
We have, $tan\dfrac{X}{2} + tan\dfrac{Z}{2} = \dfrac{2y}{x + y + z} \text{ and } s = x + y + z =$perimeter of a triangle

Apply half-angle formula and $x + y + z = s$ then,

$⇒ \dfrac{∆}{s\left(s - x\right)} + \dfrac{∆}{s\left(s - z\right)} = \dfrac{y}{s} ⇒ ∆ = \left(s - x\right)\left(s - z\right)$

$⇒ {∆}^{2} = s\left(s - x\right)\left(s - y\right)\left(s - z\right) = {\left(s - x\right)}^{2}{\left(s - z\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ {y}^{2} = {x}^{2} + {z}^{2} ⇒ ∠ Y = 90 °$

$⇒ ∠ Y = ∠ X + ∠ Z$

An option $\left(B\right)$ is correct.

Now, $\dfrac{x}{y + z} = \dfrac{sinX}{sinY + sinZ} = \dfrac{sinX}{1 + sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - X\right)} = \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{X}{2}cos\dfrac{X}{2}}{2\cos^{2}\dfrac{X}{2}} = tan\dfrac{X}{2}$

An Option $\left(C\right)$ is correct.
